proposals.title: Seeded scenario captures break while site content is uncommitted
proposals.body:
## Summary

Scenario capture on this Astro site cannot produce trustworthy frames of SEEDED app scenarios while any file under `src/content/` or `src/data/` is uncommitted. The content sandbox (`initContentSandbox` in `astro.config.mjs`, `.codeyam/tmp/content-sandbox/`) does not engage, so seeds are refused ("served committed content"). The documented workaround of stashing those files for the capture pass also failed this session: it produced frames with the chapters and communities collections EMPTY (no Chapters menu group), and `recapture-stale` reported them as clean "Recaptured". Every content-changing feature therefore ends with seeded frames that must be restored by hand and force-recaptured after the commit.

## Key Decisions

- A capture whose seed or collections did not land must fail loudly, never report "Recaptured".
- The sandbox should seed from the WORKING TREE's `src/content` when it is dirty, rather than switching off, so content edits and seeded scenarios can be captured together before the commit.

## Implementation

1. In `astro.config.mjs` (`initContentSandbox`), seed the sandbox from the working-tree `src/content`/`src/data` when dirty, and never leave a collection directory empty across a dev-server restart (the empty-collection-dir watcher bug).
2. Add a post-capture assertion for seeded app scenarios: when a collection the page renders is empty but the seed or production content has rows, fail the capture.
3. Re-verify with `harvard-in-tech-phone-menu-open` and `webinars-route-the-surviving-recordings`, which both captured empty roster frames this session.
proposals.reason: Seeded full-page screenshots came out empty or wrong but were reported as captured.

proposals.title: Screenshot staleness misses data files the page reads at runtime
proposals.body:
## What happened

This feature changed only `src/data/nav.json` (plus a few code files). The site reads that file at runtime through `readSingleton('nav.json')` in `src/lib/site.ts`, not through an import, so the screenshot staleness hash never includes it. Two seeded /donate scenarios were captured with the old menu while nav.json was stashed (the stash was needed to get the seeded captures past the dirty-content guard), and afterwards `scenario-coverage`, the strict audit and `session-finalize` Phase 3.5 all reported them as fresh. The only way to find them was to eyeball the header of each frame, and fixing them needed `recapture-stale --force --target`.

## What would have helped

Include content/data files that pages read at runtime (`src/data/*.json`, `src/content/**`) in the render-input hash, at least for application scenarios on this stack, or let `stack.json` declare runtime-read data roots. A frame that shows stale data should read as stale.
proposals.reason: Frames showing the old menu were reported fresh because nav.json is not part of the staleness hash.

proposals.title: Syncing capture scripts marks every screenshot stale
proposals.body:
## What happened

At Verify Prototype, `client-errors` refused to run because `.codeyam/capture.js` predated the binary and said to run `sync-capture-scripts`. After the sync, `scenario-coverage` reported 229 of 293 scenarios stale with reason "capture pipeline changed". The full `recapture-stale` sweep took about 38 minutes, and 247 of its captures came back pixel-identical and were restored. None of that work was related to the feature.

## What would have helped

Treat a capture-script sync as a re-verify rather than a staleness event, or let the sync record the new pipeline version without invalidating frames until a capture actually differs. At minimum, have `client-errors` and `sync-capture-scripts` warn up front that the sync makes the whole corpus stale and roughly how long the sweep will take.
proposals.reason: One required script sync turned 229 untouched scenarios stale and cost a long full sweep that changed nothing.

proposals.title: Show a compact subscribe card when the Luma calendar has nothing upcoming
proposals.body:
## Summary

The events page embeds Luma's calendar in a fixed-height frame (`src/components/LumaCalendar.astro`, `height: clamp(340px, 46vh, 540px)`). When nothing is upcoming, Luma fills that frame with its own grey "No Upcoming Events" panel, so on a phone the page shows a big, mostly empty box — the decision sheet row `m-calendar-box`, still open after the October responsive check (`docs/responsive-check-2026-10.md`, item O1). We cannot restyle inside Luma's frame, and its panel also sits ~36px inside our column on the right.

## Key Decisions

- Decide on the build side, not in the browser: the nightly-imported events collection already knows whether anything is upcoming.
- When nothing is upcoming, render the existing branded `luma-card` ("Browse & subscribe on Luma") instead of the iframe; when something is, keep the embed.
- Owner call: confirm this is wanted before building — it changes what the events page shows on quiet weeks.

## Implementation

1. `src/pages/events.astro`: compute whether the events collection has any future-dated entry and pass it to `LumaCalendar`.
2. `src/components/LumaCalendar.astro`: add a prop (e.g. `hasUpcoming`) and render the card branch when it is false even if `embedUrl` is set.
3. Scenarios: events page with and without upcoming events at Mobile, so both branches are on record.
4. Re-run `npm run check:responsive -- --only /events`.

It took a preview-flow with a real Menu click to clear it, and the flow's text-matching click on "Menu" first failed because the button also holds an icon.

## What would have helped

Only count interactions recorded at the Demo step (or explicitly marked as the demo), and let a hover used for scrolling be declared as such. A `click` text match that tolerates an icon inside the button would have saved one failed run.

proposals.title: A dead session's plan claim blocks the audit and nothing in the editor can release it
proposals.body:
## What happened

At the Reconcile step the audit failed on `SELECTED_PLAN_NOT_IN_COMPLETED` for a plan this session never touched (`remove-or-repurpose-the-unused-chapter-volunteer-link-field`). Its claim ref had been written by a session that started at 19:06 and died at once: `lastHeartbeatAt` equalled `startedAt`, the pid was gone, and there was no transcript. The finding says the claim is 'owned by this worktree' and its fixCommand archives the plan into `completed/`, which would falsely record unbuilt work as shipped.

There is no editor command to release a stale claim. Deleting the local ref did not help: the claim-sync task re-fetched it from origin within seconds. Deleting it on origin was refused by the editor's own hook (`git push is only allowed at slug(s): push`), and the harness's permission classifier also refused it as destructive. In the end the user had to run the delete by hand, and two attempts failed first because a long ref name wrapped when pasted.

## What would have helped

- A `plan-claim-release <slug>` (or `--reap-dead`) command that verifies the owning pid is dead or the heartbeat is frozen, then deletes the ref locally and on origin in one step.
- The audit finding distinguishing 'claim from a dead session' from 'archive lost on a live claim', and suggesting the release instead of the archive in the first case.
proposals.reason: Saving was blocked for several turns; the user had to delete a git ref on GitHub by hand.

proposals.title: Sort the 488 tracked files no test group owns into a group or the skip list
proposals.body:
## Summary

`codeyam-editor editor commit --out-of-workflow` and `verify-test-cache` refuse with "488 tracked file(s) are owned by no test partition and are not in testCacheIgnorePatterns". On 2026-10-15 this blocked a plan-closure commit (the work had to be committed with plain git after ending the build session). The agent-config folders were already added to the ignore list; what remains is project content: `archive/strikingly/**` (the old site snapshot), `.gitattributes`, `.gitignore`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, and others the gate only lists the first 20 of.

## Key Decisions

- Archive material, git metadata and CI files cannot change a vitest result: add them to `testCacheIgnorePatterns` in `.codeyam/editor.json` by folder glob, not file by file.
- Anything under `src/` that reaches here belongs in the vitest partition's `sourceFilePatterns` instead, so a change to it still invalidates the cache.
- Show the user the proposed glob list before writing it.

## Implementation

1. Run `codeyam-editor editor verify-test-cache` and capture the full unowned list from `.codeyam/state/command-output/verify-test-cache.txt`.
2. Group the paths by top-level folder; draft ignore globs for non-source folders and partition globs for any source paths.
3. Apply in `.codeyam/editor.json`, re-run `verify-test-cache` until it reports zero unowned files, and confirm `commit --out-of-workflow --dry-run` passes.

proposals.title: Always write alt text for images uploaded in the content editor
proposals.body:
## Summary

Images uploaded through the /admin content editor still get no real alt text. When an editor inserts an uploaded image into a blog body, the CMS falls back to the file-name stem (e.g. `img-4821`) as the alt, and image fields can be saved with the key missing. Screen-reader users hear a meaningless file name. The plan for "Fix image uploads in the content editor" asked for this and it was set aside at the approval gate.

## Key Decisions

- Always write an `alt` key. Use the editor's text, or `""` only when the editor explicitly marks the image decorative. Never omit the key and never fall back to the file name.
- Ship it through the existing `patches/@codeyam+cms+0.15.0.patch` route (see `CMS_SETUP.md`) and upstream it with the upload fixes.

## Implementation

### 1. Ask for alt text when an image is picked
**File**: `node_modules/@codeyam/cms/src/components/admin/MediaPickerModal.tsx`
After an image is selected (including the auto-select of a fresh upload), show an alt-text input with a "decorative" checkbox and pass the value along with the asset to `onSelect`.

### 2. Write it everywhere the image lands
**File**: `node_modules/@codeyam/cms/src/components/admin/EntryEditor.tsx`
In `onPickImage`, write `alt` into the field, list row or body markdown (`![alt](src)`) and drop the filename-stem fallback.
**File**: `node_modules/@codeyam/cms/src/components/admin/ImageField.tsx`
Always render and persist the `alt` key.

### 3. Tests
Extend `src/lib/mediaStagedUpload.test.tsx` to assert the body insert and the image field both carry the typed alt, and `""` only when marked decorative. Regenerate the patch with `npx patch-package @codeyam/cms`.
proposals.reason: Inserted images still get the file name as alt text, which screen readers read aloud.

proposals.title: Unseeded scenarios render the previous scenario's seeded content
proposals.body:
## What happened
On an Astro content-collection stack, scenarios that declare no `seed` (and have no `_default` tier) skip the seed adapter entirely (`decide_seed_action` -> `NoSeed`). The sandbox keeps the previous scenario's seed: after an unseeded capture, `.codeyam/tmp/content-sandbox/content` still differed from `src/content` in 12 files. The only flush attempted is `POST /api/codeyam-revalidate`, which only the Next.js template mounts. On Astro it 404s, is classified `RouteNotMounted`, and the capture proceeds. Results: `/chapters/nyc` and `/chapters/sf-bay-area` answered 404 (the previous seed had no such chapters), the London chapter page showed another scenario's photo, and committed frames carried leaked chapters ("Austin") and missing menus. All were reported as successful captures. Separately, unseeded captures take the capture gate SHARED, so at concurrency 2 they ran beside a seeding capture and photographed its seed. Workaround in this project: an `_default.json` tier with `"seed": {}` (merged_seed then returns `Flat({})`, so every scenario runs the adapter) plus `scenarios.recaptureConcurrency: 1`.

## What would have helped
Reset the content sandbox to committed content (or run the adapter with an empty seed) for every application scenario on content-collection stacks, and take the capture gate exclusively for any capture that depends on the sandbox being at baseline. Failing that, have `scenario-explain` and the capture log say that an unseeded scenario inherits whatever the previous capture left behind.
proposals.reason: A scenario with no seed never resets the content sandbox, so its screenshot shows whatever the scenario before it seeded, and the capture reports success.

proposals.title: Build commands share Vite's dependency cache with the running dev server
proposals.body:
## What happened
`verify-build` started at 19:57:57 and, nine seconds later, `node_modules/.vite/deps/react_jsx-dev-runtime.js` held React's production build, still served under the dev server's unchanged `?v=` hash. Every page with a React island then failed capture with `pageerror: jsxDEV is not a function` (cutover runbook, every CMS editor screen). `astro check` and `astro build` run with NODE_ENV=production, and their content sync runs Vite's dependency optimizer into the default cache directory, the same one the live dev server serves from. Diagnosing it took a long detour. The fix here was `cacheDir: node_modules/.vite-build` for non-dev commands (`viteCacheDir` in `src/lib/devContentRefresh.ts`).

## What would have helped
Have `verify-build` (and any editor-run build) use an isolated Vite cache, or snapshot and restore `node_modules/.vite` around it. The capture failure message could also recognise `jsxDEV is not a function` and name the likely cause (a production-mode optimizer run in the shared cache) along with the restart-plus-clear-cache recovery.
proposals.reason: verify-build ran astro check/build in production mode, which overwrote the dev server's React runtime and broke every interactive island until the dev server restarted.

proposals.title: register captures without the scenario flag that recapture-stale adds

## What happened
`recapture-stale` captures through the proxy at `:14100/<path>?_codeyam_scenario=<slug>`, but `register @<scenario>.json` captures directly at `:4321/<path>` with no flag. This project turns off its hero carousel's autoplay when that flag is present, so `register` captured `hero-carousel` on whichever slide the timer had reached (slide 2), while the sweep captured slide 1. Three captures of one unchanged scenario produced three different frames.

## What would have helped
One capture path, with the same URL and flags, whether a scenario is captured by `register`, `recapture-stale` or the preview. At minimum, `register` should append the same scenario flag.
proposals.reason: The same scenario renders differently under register and recapture-stale, because only recapture adds ?_codeyam_scenario to the capture URL.
